title: Cheque Image and Signature Mismatch Flagging
summary: Compare inward CTS cheque images with specimen signatures, mandates and Positive Pay data, and rank cheques by risk so verification officers look first where it matters.

seo.title: Cheque Signature Mismatch Flagging with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision for inward clearing: compares cheque signatures with specimens, checks amount, date and Positive Pay data, and ranks items for officers.

problem.intro: In cheque truncation the drawee bank sees only images, and must confirm signature, amount, date and mandate before the return deadline. As CTS moves to continuous clearing with settlement on realisation, that window gets shorter, while officers still compare signatures by eye against scanned specimen cards.

pain_points.title: Signature checks against poor specimens
pain_points.detail: Specimen signatures scanned years ago, sometimes from branch cards, make visual comparison slow and subjective.

pain_points.title: Mandate and joint-account rules
pain_points.detail: Cheques on joint and corporate accounts need the right combination of signatories, which officers must look up for each item.

pain_points.title: Amount and date errors
pain_points.detail: Mismatches between amount in words and figures, stale or post-dated cheques and alterations are easy to miss at volume.

pain_points.title: Uniform effort on uneven risk
pain_points.detail: Every cheque gets similar attention, although high-value items, new payees and long-inactive accounts carry far more risk.

solution.overview: We build a verification assistant for inward clearing. For each cheque image it reads the MICR band, date, payee and the amount in figures and words, and locates the signature area. A signature comparison model scores similarity against the specimens in your signature repository, and a rules layer checks the operating mandate, account status, stop-payment instructions, cheque series and any Positive Pay details the customer submitted. Cheques are ranked by combined risk and value, and the verification officer sees the cheque, the specimens and every flag side by side. The officer decides to pass or return every item; the assistant never returns a cheque on its own.
capabilities: Reads MICR, date, payee and amounts in figures and words from CTS images, including handwriting
Signature similarity scoring against one or more specimens per signatory
Mandate checks for joint, either-or-survivor and corporate signatory rules
Positive Pay, stop-payment, cheque series and account status checks
Detection of alterations, overwriting and amount-in-words mismatches
Risk-ranked queue combining value, flags and account context

workflow.title: Receive inward images
workflow.detail: Inward clearing images and data arrive from the CTS interface into the bank's inward processing system.

workflow.title: Read the cheque
workflow.detail: OCR and handwriting recognition read the date, payee, amounts and MICR fields, and the signature region is located.

workflow.title: Compare and check
workflow.detail: Signatures are scored against specimens, and mandate, Positive Pay, stop-payment and account status checks run.

workflow.title: Rank by risk
workflow.detail: Each cheque gets a risk band with reasons, combining flags, value and account context.

workflow.title: Officer verification
workflow.detail: Officers review high-risk items first with cheque and specimens side by side, and record pass or return with a reason code.

workflow.title: Return and learn
workflow.detail: Decisions flow back to the inward system, and confirmed mismatches feed periodic threshold reviews.

inputs: Inward clearing cheque images, front and back
MICR and presentment data from the clearing interface
Positive Pay submissions and stop-payment instructions
Account status and issued cheque series from core banking
outputs: Signature similarity scores with specimen references
Flags for mandate, alteration, date, amount and Positive Pay mismatches
Officer decisions with reason codes and audit trail
human_in_the_loop: Verification officers make every pass or return decision, with high-risk items shown first. Signature similarity is a decision aid; the bank's signature verification policy and the officer's judgement prevail.
integrations: Inward clearing or CTS processing system
Core banking for account status, mandates and cheque series
Positive Pay data from the bank's channels
guardrails: No automatic returns; officers decide every cheque
Return reason codes always chosen by the officer
Thresholds tuned per customer segment and reviewed with fraud risk
Images and account data stay inside the bank's environment
Score drift monitored when specimen quality or scanner sources change
compliance_notes: Works within the bank's CTS procedures and RBI's Positive Pay arrangements; the drawee bank's verification responsibility stays with its officers.
Supports RBI IT governance expectations by processing images on bank-controlled infrastructure.

pilot.scope: Historical inward clearing images from one processing centre, including known returned and fraud items, scored offline and compared with officer decisions.
deliverables: Field extraction and signature scoring on historical images
Mandate and Positive Pay rule set
Comparison report against officer decisions and known fraud cases
Production plan aligned with your clearing timelines

what_we_measure.how: Known returned-for-signature and fraud items placed in the high-risk band, measured on historical data.
Genuine cheques placed in the high-risk band, reviewed with officers.
Extracted date, amount and payee compared with officer-verified values.
Timed for officers using the side-by-side screen against their current process.

faqs.q: Can the model return a cheque?
faqs.a: No. It ranks and flags. Officers decide pass or return and choose the reason code, as your clearing procedures require.

faqs.q: Our specimen signatures are old scans. Will it still work?
faqs.a: Specimen quality affects accuracy, so the pilot reports results by specimen quality and lists accounts where re-capturing the specimen would help. Comparisons against poor specimens are marked as low confidence rather than scored with false certainty.

faqs.q: Does this fit within clearing deadlines?
faqs.a: Scoring runs as images arrive, before officers start verification, so it adds no step to the critical path. We size the infrastructure against your peak inward volumes during the pilot.
On infrastructure the bank controls, either on-premise or in its private cloud. Images and signature data do not leave that environment.
